# A pure js: function that throws costs its own value and no other: the two
# calls share one node run, the runtime records the throw against that one key,
# and the compiler reads the key's absence out of the results document the run
# still produced. An `exit status` here would mean the throw escaped its call
# and took the other one's value down with it.
#
# html reaches js through the bundler, not through a language that names the
# scheme, so schemeRunnableAtRuntime says this target cannot recompute the
# value: the missing key aborts the build rather than shipping a page with a
# hole in it.
[!node] skip
env SNGL_CONSTEVAL_CACHE=$WORK/evalcache

! sngl generate --lang=none --platform=html --out=out app.sngl
stderr 'consteval: .*: nope'
stderr 'lib\.boom'
stderr 'compile-time evaluation of boom produced no value'
! stderr 'exit status'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import lib "js:./lib"

const bad = lib.boom()
const good = lib.fine()

component main {
    text(value=bad)
    text(value=good)
}
-- lib/index.ts --
/** @sngl-pure */
export function boom(): string {
    throw new Error("nope");
}

/** @sngl-pure */
export function fine(): string {
    return "ok";
}
